root_causes: A green PR verification/promotion label was verification-only and did not itself prove a production deploy.

The original writer reconciliation required release.json commit_ref to equal the writer merge SHA exactly, so a later production commit that legitimately contained the writer merge could not close the older writer outcome.
The approved-central writer branch family was not handled by the Notion reconciliation case statement.

Earlier candidate delivery exposed additional structural defects: JSON-array output was treated as JSONL, the first source hash used Markdown rather than Notion plain_text, generated pages missed FAQPage/figure SEO contracts, external Google Fonts hurt Lighthouse performance, bot-created PRs produced action_required runs with zero jobs, and generator-only changes were misclassified as requiring a site preview.
required_future_behavior: A Powerhouse content outcome may become delivered only after the canonical host proves a production commit that contains the governed content merge and content readback succeeds. A newer descendant production commit is valid evidence for an older writer merge. Reconciliation must then update the existing canonical outcome/queue/learning lineage; never create a parallel delivery ledger.
